newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed, Molten Metal study M4 changes.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed, Molten Metal study M4 changes.

text.p: Molten Metal Technology Inc said Wednesday it and Lockheed Martin Corp intend to explore the restructuring of M4 Environmental LP, a limited partnership jointly owned by the two corporations.
The parties intend to finalize any restructuring by April, subject to completion of legal documentation and regulatory approvals, Molten Metal said.
The company also said Millard S. Firebaugh has been named president and chief executive officer of M4, effective immediately.

It said J. Robert Merriman, who has served as president and chief executive officer of M4 since the partnership was established in 1994, will be working with Lockheed's Al Narath, president and chief operating officer of the Energy and Environmental Sector, and Molten Metal's William M. Haney, president and chief executive officer, to assess new business opportunities and long-range strategies for the corporations' environmental business pursuits.
Firebaugh joined M4 in June of 1996 as technical director responsible for integrating advanced technology and services.
Prior to joining M4, he served in the U.S. Navy for 35 years, where he managed the SEAWOLF Class submarine program.
Molten Metal said the objective of any restructuring would be to eliminate many of the organizational redundancies associated with the limited partnership.

"Historically, our partnership with Lockheed Martin has evolved to keep pace with changes in the marketplace, and now that we have made significant headway into several key markets, we need to adapt to continue optimizing the strengths of each party," said Molten Metal's William M. Haney.
"Steps to restructure will enable us to more effectively leverage Molten Metal's discriminating proprietary technologies," noted Lockheed's Narath.
The limited partnership currently operates a commercial system in Oak Ridge, Tenn., with a second commercial system set to begin operations there in the first quarter of 1997.

M4 was formed in 1994 by Martin Marietta Corp and Molten Metal to commercialize that company's catalytic extraction processing technology. In 1995, Martin Marietta merged with Lockheed, forming Lockheed Martin. After the merger, Lockheed Martin and Molten Metal reorganized M4 to take advantage of Lockheed's environmental business expertise.
